title: SAC ledger: historical tampering is undetected when a same-size rewrite lands in the same filesystem timestamp tick

AC1.note: A same-size rewrite with unchanged mtimeNs/ctimeNs is now detected: the content digest changes. Merged as fe0431fc.

AC2.note: The four stat fields are removed from the checkpoint entirely and identityMatches is deleted; trust derives from a sha256 over the audited ledger prefix, not from the filesystem's opinion about when the file changed.

AC3.note: The test passes deterministically: 5 consecutive isolated runs green on the branch and 5 more on main after merge, against 6 consecutive red on the pre-fix code. Not quarantined, not weakened.

AC4.note: Mutation: deleting the single digest-comparison line in fastCheckpointState turned the named test red 3/3 in isolation and took the new mid-ledger test with it. Restored and re-verified.

AC5.note: The fast path stays one sequential read plus one sha256. The assumption is stated at the code: identical bytes yield identical records because the audit splits on newlines and JSON-parses each line, both deterministic, so byte equality with an audited snapshot is as strong as re-running that audit.

AC6.note: Detection covers the whole audited prefix, so an edit at index 0, mid-ledger or at the tail is equally visible. A new test corrupts the middle record of a three-record ledger. The chain alone could not do this: a mid-ledger edit leaves every stored hash byte-identical, so the link check passes.

AC7.note: A v1.0 checkpoint fails parsing on both key set and version, so it is re-audited from scratch and rewritten as 1.1, never trusted under the new rule. A tampered ledger under a hand-forged, correctly-hashed legacy checkpoint is refused rather than adopted.

AC8.note: Divergence refuses rather than falling back: a short file or digest mismatch throws. Falling back to a full audit would let a clean truncation to a valid prefix pass as a healthy, merely shorter ledger, because the audit cannot know how long the ledger should be.

AC9.note: typecheck clean; bun test 6279 pass / 18 skip / 0 fail against a 6275/0 baseline; test:guards 173/0; check:doc-links 1138 links / 0 broken; the previously nondeterministic test green across five consecutive isolated runs.
